shadows.name: panel

narrative.overview:
Instruments and field notes laid out on warm paper. A surveyor's desk is dense because the work is dense, and calm because every object on it has a job and a place. Nothing is decorative. Everything is legible at a glance, and the things that need attention are the things you notice first.

Pounce shows a technical SEO crawl: hundreds of thousands of rows, thirty checks per page, four levels of severity. The interface exists to make that legible without making it loud. It is warm rather than cool, because the previous cool blue-black build read as a TUI tool made for hackers to the person who specified it. Warmth here is not softness: the density is unchanged.

This system explicitly rejects the terminal, and equally rejects the SaaS marketing register.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral stack, every grey tinted toward the brand hue (283.5 degrees).
A single accent, used only to mark the current thing.
Severity is the loudest signal on screen, and never carried by colour alone.
Four type steps, each with its own tracking and leading.
Flat by region, lifted only where something genuinely floats.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent marks the current thing: the selected row, the active tab, the applied filter, the focused control. Never decoration. Well under ten percent of the surface, and that rarity is what makes a selection findable in a table of a million rows.

rules.name: The Severity Band Rule
rules.body: The brand colour is forbidden from the red, amber and green band. This has survived two complete redesigns and outranks any aesthetic preference.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every severity is drawn with an icon and a word beside its hue. Remove the colour and the interface must still be correct.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries chroma 0.004 to 0.014 at hue 283.5. Pure grey, #ffffff and #000000 are forbidden, and a neutral tinted away from the accent is the specific failure this rule prevents.

rules.name: The Three Steps Rule
rules.body: Three sizes — 11 / 13 / 16 — at ratios 1.18 and 1.23. The scale before the redesign put three of its five steps within two pixels of each other and everything read at one volume. The fourth step, 20px, was cut in T4.64: it had exactly one consumer in the whole app. A step used once is a decoration, not a level. Adding a fourth requires naming its second consumer first.

rules.name: The Size Owns Its Tracking Rule
rules.body: Tracking and leading are properties of the size step, never global. A single global letter-spacing is wrong for at least one size by definition.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for text read character by character. Counts, sizes and percentages need tabular figures on Inter instead. Forty-two monospaced fragments in one window is what a terminal looks like.

rules.name: The Flat Until It Floats Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only if it genuinely sits above the content: the detail pane and a modal dialog. Every other region is tonal.

rules.name: The Press Goes Down Rule
rules.body: Active removes the control shadow and darkens the ground. A pressed control must read as pressed, not as hovered harder.

rules.name: The Scale Is Six Values Rule
rules.body: Padding and gaps come from 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 and nothing between. Before T4.64 there were twenty distinct padding tokens and fourteen gap tokens, with 2px, 6px and 10px sitting beside 4px, 8px and 12px — none wrong alone, and no two panels agreeing on what "tight" meant. `npm run check:spacing` fails the build on the next off-scale class, because a scale kept by memory is a scale that lasts one feature.

dos: Do author every colour in OKLCH, and tint every neutral toward hue 283.5 at chroma 0.004 to 0.014.
Do pair every severity colour with an icon and a word.
Do give each type step its own tracking and leading.
Do use .nums (Inter tabular figures) for anything that must line up, and reserve .tabular (JetBrains Mono) for URLs, paths and canonicals.
Do run npm run check:contrast after any palette change. It parses OKLCH, throws on an unparseable colour rather than scoring it, and fails the build.
Do list a check that found nothing, at zero, greyed.
Do write findings as sentences from the rule registry's own description.
Do keep gutters uniform. Predictable grids are an affordance at this density.
donts: Don't make it look like a TUI tool made for hackers. No near-black grounds, no monospace as a default voice, no hairline radii, no single-plane flatness.
Don't move the accent into the red, amber or green band, ever.
Don't use pure #ffffff, #000000, or any untinted grey.
Don't use monospace for counts, sizes, durations or percentages.
Don't add a fifth type step without deleting one.
Don't use em dashes in interface copy. Parentheses for qualifiers, colons or periods for clauses.
Don't reinvent a standard affordance. No custom scrollbars, no bespoke form controls, no hand-rolled modals.
Don't remove a focus outline without putting something in its place.
Don't give a region a shadow because it looks flat. Ask whether it floats.
Don't use border-left above one pixel as a coloured accent stripe, gradient text, glassmorphism, hero-metric layouts, or identical card grids.
Don't show a rule id where a finding belongs.
